A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MoRAM research. All 30 pages of v3 and 29 pages of v5, including appendices, are readable. Equations, experiments, tables and figures can be matched despite extensive reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original MoRAM experiments on CLIP and language models, including benchmark results, routing ablations, pruning experiments and activation analyses.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, temperature and load-balancing controls, and latency measurements.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.3 retain the same rank-1 memory experts, self-activation, top-k selection, temperature scaling, inference thresholding, incremental expansion and optional pruning. The standard training objective is unchanged; the added regularization and temperature variants are experimental controls.

E1.justification: Both versions cover X-TAIL, MTIL, TRACE, standard and 15-task language continual learning, SuperNI, and CodeAlpaca fine-tuning evaluated on HumanEval and MMLU. The added comparisons and analyses use existing datasets and task coverage.

E2.justification: v5 Table 15 adds evaluated X-TAIL comparators NoRGa and SD-LoRA; SD-LoRA was cited but not evaluated in v3. Table 4 also adds a temperature-tuned coarse MoE-LoRA comparator. The earlier comparison methods are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix A.1 changes the reported CLIP temperature from 0.1 to 0.01 and TRACE learning rate from 1e-4 to 5e-4. New protocols include an eight-temperature coarse-baseline sweep and latency measurements after tasks 1, 5 and 10. These documented changes do not establish that the retained benchmark experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v5 adds targeted tests of whether temperature tuning helps coarse experts (Table 4), whether load balancing helps MoRAM on X-TAIL and 15-task T5 learning (Table 22), and how latency grows with accumulated tasks (Table 20). Existing pruning, order-robustness, sparsity and activation analyses remain.

E5.justification: Three-run mean and standard-deviation reporting in Tables 2 and 16 is retained, as is variability across task orders in v3 Table 14 and v5 Table 17. No new run counts, uncertainty-estimation procedures or significance tests are documented.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation values are retained. Newly reported entries include NoRGa/SD-LoRA aggregate Last accuracy of 69.0/74.3 on X-TAIL (Table 15), temperature-tuned coarse MoE-LoRA Last accuracy of 74.57 (Table 4), MoRAM inference latency rising from 2.07 to 2.52 ms/image after tasks 1 to 10 (Table 20), and load-balanced MoRAM Last accuracy of 77.3 versus 80.9 without that regularizer (Table 22).

T1.justification: The associative-memory definition, static key–value remark, method equations (1)–(8), and OP/BWT equations (9)–(10) are mathematically unchanged. Definition and remark renumbering introduces no new assumptions, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about atomic associative memory, router-free sparse retrieval, improved plasticity–stability, generalization and reduced forgetting. The rewritten abstract and additional evidence do not redefine the core contribution.

C2.justification: v5 adds explanations that sharpening coarse experts cannot separate their mixed knowledge (Section 4.3), uniform load balancing conflicts with uneven semantic frequencies (C.6), and relevance computation grows with accumulated atoms despite sparse activation (C.4). Existing future-work qualifications and storage/pruning tradeoffs remain.

D1.justification: v5 adds a project-page link and makes the CLIP temperature disclosure consistent with Section 4.3. It revises TRACE's learning-rate disclosure but removes its explicit epoch sequence {2, 1, 3, 2, 1, 2, 2, 3} without replacement. Most other implementation and hardware details are retained.

R1.justification: Citation additions include Brown et al. on in-context learning, Le et al. on NoRGa, and several newer replay and MoE works. Appendix B.4 adds brief positioning against NoRGa and the previously cited SD-LoRA. The central associative-memory and fine-grained-expert novelty argument remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3's single appendix with Sections A.1–A.13 is reorganized into four thematic appendices covering experimental details, additional results, analyses/ablations and visualizations, with substantial section reordering. The abstract is rewritten, accompanied by smaller wording, author-name and funding edits.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column proceedings document, with widespread resizing and relocation of tables and figures. Table 4 gains coarse/fine-grained groupings and a control row; Tables 15, 20 and 22 are added. All ten original figures retain their graphical content.

improvement.justification: The temperature-controlled coarse baseline, load-balancing ablation and measured latency better support the existing design and efficiency claims. Appendix reorganization and consistent CLIP temperature documentation also improve usability. These are limited net gains, tempered by removal of TRACE's epoch schedule and an unexplained learning-rate revision while its reported results remain unchanged.
